instructions.name: accept_ownership
docs: Accepts a pending ownership transfer, making the caller the new pool owner.
Shared function signature used by all CCIP token pool programs.

instructions.name: append_remote_pool_addresses
docs: Appends additional remote pool addresses to an existing ChainConfig.
Reallocates the PDA to accommodate the extra entries.

instructions.name: configure_allow_list
docs: Adds addresses to the allow-list and/or enables the allow-list check.
When enabled, only listed addresses may send tokens through the pool.

instructions.name: delete_chain_config
docs: Closes and reclaims rent from a ChainConfig PDA.
After this call no cross-chain messages can be sent to or from that chain.

instructions.name: delete_chain_config_override
docs: Closes and reclaims rent from a ChainConfigOverride PDA.

instructions.name: derive_accounts_lock_or_burn_tokens
docs: Called by the router via CPI during `DeriveAccountsCcipSend` to discover
any extra accounts needed for the onramp token transfer.
Lockrelease pools have no additional account requirements beyond the
standard token lookup table, so this returns an empty set.

instructions.name: derive_accounts_release_or_mint_tokens
docs: Called by the offramp via CPI during `DeriveAccountsExecute` to discover
any extra accounts needed for the offramp token transfer.
Lockrelease pools have no additional account requirements beyond the
standard token lookup table, so this returns an empty set.

instructions.name: edit_chain_remote_config
docs: Overwrites the remote config (token address and pool addresses) for an
existing ChainConfig. Reallocates the PDA if the new config is larger.

instructions.name: get_pool_fee
docs: Returns the fee receipt for a token transfer.

accounts.name: chain_config_v2
docs: May or may not be initialized

accounts.name: chain_config_v2
docs: When initialized (owner == this program)

instructions.name: init_chain_config_override
docs: Initializes a ChainConfigOverride PDA for the given remote chain and override type.
Used to set separate rate limit buckets (e.g. for faster-than-finality transfers).

accounts.name: mint
docs: The token this pool wraps. Needed to create the fee vault ATA the lane's in-token BPS fee
accrues into.

accounts.name: fee_vault_token_account
docs: The fee vault's ATA for the pool's own mint, where `lock_or_burn_tokens_v2` accrues the
in-token BPS fee. Created here so that configuring a
lane and being able to collect (and withdraw) its BPS fee are the same operation.

instructions.name: init_chain_remote_config
docs: Initializes a ChainConfig PDA for the given remote chain.
Must be called before any cross-chain messages can be sent to or from
that chain. Remote pool addresses are added separately via
append_remote_pool_addresses.

instructions.name: init_global_config
docs: Initializes the program-level PoolConfig PDA.
Must be called once by the program's upgrade authority before any
token pool can be created.

instructions.name: initialize
docs: Creates a new per-mint State PDA for the given mint.
The upgrade authority (or a mint authority when self-serve is enabled)
becomes the pool owner.

instructions.name: initialize_by_multisig
docs: Creates a new per-mint State PDA for the given mint via a mint authority multisig signer.
Self-serve must be enabled. Only 1-of-N multisigs are supported.

accounts.name: mint_authority_multisig
docs: Only 1-of-N SPL Token multisigs are supported here.

instructions.name: lock_or_burn_tokens
docs: Locks tokens from the sender's account as part of an outbound
cross-chain transfer. Called by the router via CPI after the onramp
has validated the message.

instructions.name: lock_or_burn_tokens_v2
docs: Locks tokens in the pool as part of an outbound cross-chain transfer (V2).

accounts.name: chain_config_v2
docs: May or may not be initialized; read via `ChainConfigV2::try_load`, defaulting to
`WAIT_FOR_FINALITY` (full-finality only) when absent. The router supplies this account for
every v2 pool transfer, and its position (between `chain_config` and `chain_config_override`)
must mirror the router's `transfer_token_v2` CPI account order and the resolver's
`accounts_to_save` order.

accounts.name: chain_config_override
docs: When initialized (owner == this program), its rate limit buckets
override the default ones for faster-than-finality transfers.

accounts.name: fee_vault_token_account
docs: token-pool receipt fees into. In-token BPS fees accrue here until the owner withdraws them
with `withdraw_fee_tokens`; keeping them here rather than in `pool_token_account` is what
makes fees distinguishable from the locked liquidity. The vault PDA is derived inline rather
than passed in: it holds no data and never signs here, and every account this instruction
takes costs 32 bytes of a `ccip_send` transaction that is already close to the size limit.

instructions.name: nested_resolve_accounts_start
docs: Resolves the accounts needed for V2 lock_or_burn or release_or_mint
instructions based on the instruction discriminator.

instructions.name: observe_chain_config
docs: Returns a pool's configuration for a single remote chain, for observability consumers.
Rate limiter buckets are reported as of now, i.e. including the refill accrued since the
last transfer.
Permissionless and read-only: meant to be executed through `simulateTransaction`. Fails if
the lane has no chain config, which callers can read as "not configured".

instructions.name: observe_chain_config_override
docs: Returns a pool's rate limit override for a single remote chain and override type, for
observability consumers. Rate limiter buckets are reported as of now, i.e. including the
refill accrued since the last transfer.
Permissionless and read-only: meant to be executed through `simulateTransaction`. Fails if
the lane has no override of that type, which callers can read as "not overridden".

instructions.name: observe_chain_config_v2
docs: Returns a pool's CCIP 2.0 CCV configuration for a single remote chain, for observability
consumers.
Permissionless and read-only: meant to be executed through `simulateTransaction`. Fails if
the lane has no CCV config, which callers can read as "not configured".

instructions.name: observe_state
docs: Returns a pool's per-mint configuration, for observability consumers.
Permissionless and read-only: meant to be executed through `simulateTransaction`. The
allow list is reported as a count only.

instructions.name: provide_liquidity
docs: Rebalancer adds liquidity to the pool's token account.

instructions.name: release_or_mint_tokens
docs: Releases tokens to the receiver's account as part of an inbound
cross-chain transfer. Called by the offramp via CPI after the
message has been verified and committed.

accounts.name: offramp_program
docs: CHECK offramp program: exists only to derive the allowed offramp PDA
and the authority PDA.

accounts.name: allowed_offramp
docs: CHECK PDA of the router program verifying the signer is an allowed offramp.
If PDA does not exist, the router doesn't allow this offramp

instructions.name: release_or_mint_tokens_v2
docs: Releases tokens to the receiver as part of an inbound cross-chain transfer (V2).

accounts.name: offramp_program
docs: CHECK offramp program: exists only to derive the allowed offramp PDA
and the authority PDA.

accounts.name: allowed_offramp
docs: CHECK PDA of the router program verifying the signer is an allowed offramp.
If PDA does not exist, the router doesn't allow this offramp

accounts.name: chain_config_override
docs: When initialized (owner == this program), its rate limit buckets
override the default ones for faster-than-finality transfers.

instructions.name: remove_from_allow_list
docs: Removes addresses from the allow-list.

instructions.name: set_chain_config_override_rate_limit
docs: Updates the rate limits on a ChainConfigOverride PDA.
Callable by the pool owner or the rate-limit admin.

instructions.name: set_chain_rate_limit
docs: Updates the inbound and outbound rate limits for a specific remote chain.
Callable by either the pool owner or the rate-limit admin.

instructions.name: set_rate_limit_admin
docs: Sets the rate-limit admin for a token pool.
The rate-limit admin may call set_chain_rate_limit without being the pool owner.

instructions.name: set_rebalancer
docs: Sets the rebalancer address for the pool.
If the rebalancer is the default address then no rebalance is allowed.

instructions.name: set_rmn
docs: Updates the RMN Remote address on an individual token pool's State.
Only callable by the upgrade authority if they also own the pool.

instructions.name: set_router
docs: Updates the router address on an individual token pool's State.
Changes the expected signer for lock/burn and release/mint calls.
Only callable by the upgrade authority if they also own the pool.

instructions.name: transfer_ownership
docs: Initiates an ownership transfer for this token pool to a new proposed owner.
The proposed owner must call accept_ownership to complete the handover.

instructions.name: type_version
docs: Returns the program type (name) and version string encoded at build time.
Offchain code calls this to confirm which program and version is deployed
before sending any other instruction.

instructions.name: update_default_rmn
docs: Updates the default RMN Remote address stored in PoolConfig.
New token pools created after this call will use the new RMN Remote.

instructions.name: update_default_router
docs: Updates the default router address stored in PoolConfig.
New token pools created after this call will use the new router.

instructions.name: update_self_served_allowed
docs: Enables or disables self-served pool initialization.
When enabled, any mint authority may create a pool for their mint
without requiring the program upgrade authority.

instructions.name: withdraw_fee_tokens
docs: Sweeps the fees this pool accrued for `mint` in a single fee token into a recipient token
account of the pool owner's choosing. Restricted to the pool owner.
If `amount` is provided, only the requested amount is transferred. Otherwise (if None) the
entire balance is transferred.

accounts.name: mint
docs: The token this pool wraps. Unrelated to `fee_token_mint`, but part of the fee vault seeds.

accounts.name: recipient
docs: Where the fees go. Freely chosen by the pool owner, unlike the executor and the CCVs, which
pin the destination to a `fee_aggregator` held in their config.

accounts.name: fee_token_mint
docs: The token the fees were billed in, which is whatever the sender paid with, so a pool
accrues one vault ATA per fee token it has ever been paid in.

instructions.name: withdraw_liquidity
docs: Rebalancer withdraws liquidity from the pool's token account.
Can be used to transfer liquidity from one pool to another by setting
the `rebalancer` to the calling pool.

fields.name: rebalancer
docs: Set the rebalancer address for the pool; if set to the default "no rebalance" address
(Pubkey::default()), no rebalance is allowed.

fields.name: can_accept_liquidity
docs: DEPRECATED: this field is no longer enforced at runtime. It is kept for backward
compatibility (no PDA migration) and is always initialized to `true`.
To disable inflows operationally, set the rebalancer to `Pubkey::default()`.

fields.name: allowed_finality_config
docs: Allowed finality policy for *outbound* (lock_or_burn) transfers on this lane.
Mirrors EVM's pool-wide `s_allowedFinalityConfig`. Zero-initialized
(`WAIT_FOR_FINALITY`) means only full-finality transfers are permitted.

types.name: FinalityConfig
docs: Per-message finality configuration. Wire-format: 4 bytes big-endian (flags || block_depth).
Mirrors the `bytes4` Finality type in chainlink-ccv's `protocol/finality.go`.
Layout (MSB first):
flags[15:1]  — reserved
flags[0]     — S: wait for `safe` head instead of full finality
block_depth  — number of block confirmations required (0 = full finality / safe, per flags)

fields.name: amount
docs: Token amount used to determine the required CCVs.
For inbound transfers, the amount is denominated in the remote token's decimals
and must be converted to local token decimals before applying amount-based CCV
policies. For outbound transfers, the amount is already denominated in local
token decimals, but is the gross amount before the pool's in-token BPS fee: the
pool deducts that fee before applying amount-based CCV policies, as it only sends
the post-fee remainder cross-chain. Inbound amounts are already post-fee.

fields.name: msg_total_nonce
docs: DEPRECATED. The onramp's full nonce for this message, keyed by `original_sender` and
`remote_chain_selector`. Still populated with a real value by the 1.6 onramp
(`ccip-router`'s `instructions_v1/v1/onramp.rs`), but hard-coded to `0` by `ccip_send_v2`,
which no longer tracks per-sender nonces.
The only pool that reads it is `cctp-token-pool`, which uses it as a PDA seed for the
`cctp_message_sent_event` account (see that program's `lib.rs` and `derive.rs`). A constant
`0` would therefore collide across messages — so the `0` is only sound because a CCTP v1 pool
can never be reached from `ccip_send_v2`:
- CCTP and Lombard are the only v1 pools that set `implements_account_resolution`.
- `TokenTransferContext::new` (the router's `instructions/common.rs`) verifies the
`TokenAdminRegistry` PDA and then rejects `interface_version == 1` &&
`implements_account_resolution` with `UnsupportedPoolV1ResolutionOnLaneV2`. That runs in
`ccip_send_v2` before any pool CPI, so it is the authoritative gate; the account-resolution
stage (`ccip_send/resolve_accounts/token_transfer_static.rs`) rejects the same combination
earlier, but is only advisory since callers can build the transaction themselves.
- `set_pool_interface_implementation` additionally refuses to register
`implements_account_resolution` below `interface_version` 2. The runtime check still
matters because registries migrated from 1.6 can carry the v1/resolution combination.
Removing the field outright is a breaking change to the v1 pool interface, so it stays until
the 1.6 lane is retired. Anything that starts consuming it must not assume it is meaningful
on the v2 lane.

types.name: MessageDirection
docs: Direction of a cross-chain message, used for CCV requirements.

types.name: NestedResolveAccountsParams
docs: Resolution parameters used by nested resolvers. Rather than the full ix_data and a metadata
field, they have an opaque `cpi_resolution_inputs` field that doubles as both. The caller
of the nested resolution is responsible for correctly encoding it by consulting
the documentation.

fields.name: caller
docs: The account expected to sign the final instruction being resolved.

fields.name: caller_program
docs: The program ID that derived `caller` and is driving this resolution (the router on the
send side, the offramp on the execute side).

fields.name: cpi_resolution_inputs
docs: Will be deserialized into a type the nested resolver understands. For what to
send in the first stage of nested resolution, consult the nested resolver's documentation.

fields.name: ask_again_with
docs: In the next resolution round, call the resolution method
including these accounts (all read-only).

fields.name: accounts_to_save
docs: Append these accounts to a separate accumulator list. Once
`next_ix_discriminator` is empty, this accumulated list
contains all accounts for the instruction of interest.

fields.name: lookup_tables_to_save
docs: Append these lookup tables to a separate accumulator list.
Once resolution is complete, the accumulated list contains all
LUTs that the instruction of interest can use.

fields.name: next_cpi_resolution_inputs
docs: If nonempty, perform another resolution stage with these inputs.

types.name: PoolChainConfigObservation
docs: Per-remote-chain configuration of a token pool, as observed by off-chain consumers.

fields.name: remote_token_address
docs: Token address on the remote chain, as raw bytes.

fields.name: remote_pool_addresses
docs: Pool addresses on the remote chain, as raw bytes. More than one entry means earlier pool
versions are still accepted as sources.

types.name: PoolChainConfigOverrideObservation
docs: Per-remote-chain, per-override-type rate limit override of a token pool, as observed by
off-chain consumers.
Override PDAs are optional: when a lane has no override of the requested type, the observing
instruction fails, which callers can read as "not overridden".

fields.name: override_type
docs: Which flavour of transfer this override applies to (e.g. fast transfers).

types.name: PoolChainConfigV2Observation
docs: Per-remote-chain CCIP 2.0 configuration of a token pool, as observed by off-chain consumers.

fields.name: threshold_amount
docs: Transfer amount above which the threshold CCVs are additionally required. Zero disables the
threshold lists.

fields.name: allowed_finality_config
docs: Allowed finality policy for outbound (lock_or_burn) transfers on this lane.

types.name: PoolStateObservation
docs: Per-mint configuration of a token pool, as observed by off-chain consumers.
The allow list is reported as a count only, as its size is unbounded by configuration.

fields.name: rebalancer
docs: Rebalancer, only meaningful for lock/release pools. The default pubkey means rebalancing is
not allowed.

types.name: ProtocolAmount
docs: CCIP 2.0 compatible cross-chain amount representation (u256 in big-endian bytes, based
on abi.encodePacked)

types.name: RateLimiterObservation
docs: State of one rate limiter bucket, as of the moment of observation.

fields.name: tokens
docs: Tokens available now: the stored balance plus the refill accrued since the bucket was last
touched, capped at `capacity`. This is the value EVM's `getCurrent*RateLimiterState`
returns, not the raw stored balance.

fields.name: last_updated
docs: Timestamp the `tokens` value corresponds to (the observation time, for an enabled bucket).

fields.name: source_pool_address
docs: @dev WARNING: sourcePoolAddress should be checked prior to any processing of funds. Make sure it matches the
expected pool address for the given remoteChainSelector.

fields.name: offchain_token_data
docs: @dev WARNING: offchainTokenData is untrusted data.

fields.name: allowed_finality_config
docs: Allowed finality policy for outbound (lock_or_burn) transfers on this lane.
`WAIT_FOR_FINALITY` (zero) permits only full-finality transfers.
